errors.text: The powder-extrusion printing route is incorrectly replaced by immediate hot extrusion; hydrogen de-binding, prolonged vacuum sintering, and the titanium-sponge oxygen getter are omitted.
The proposed 400–600°C decomposition and 1100–1200°C extrusion schedule conflicts with sintering at 1400°C for 18 hours and subsequent water quenching from 1500°C.
The hypothesis treats oxygen exclusion as the objective, whereas the target requires controlled oxygen near 1.0 wt.% for interstitial strengthening while avoiding excessive alpha-HCP formation.
It omits the decisive rapid-quench step needed to suppress alpha-HCP precipitation and retain metastable beta-BCC.
The ultra-high-vacuum requirement of less than 10^-7 Pa is unsupported and substantially more stringent than the demonstrated vacuum condition.
Sequential hydride decomposition and in-situ alloying governed by hydride formation enthalpies are not reconstructed.
